abstract: We give a bounded algebraic procedure for transporting a nonzero mixed surface class to four specified primitive CM abelian factors. The input consists of actual source maps to isotypic CM quotients, compatible target polarizations, and a nonzero mixed pairing; the output is a finite family of Hom graphs with a checkable success locus. If $E$ has degree $2g$, a quotient $B$ has dimension $d=gm$, and $\theta:B^\vee\to B$ is the polarization induced by an ample source divisor, the integral pairing $T(f,h)=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_1(B,\mathbb Q)}(\theta f^\vee\lambda_Jh)$ has determinant $|\operatorname{disc}E|^m\deg(\lambda_J)^m\deg(\theta)$. Its diagonal is exactly twice the source divisor degree of the pulled-back target polarization. Minkowski therefore bounds a rational spanning family, its graph Hilbert polynomials, and a surviving image surface's degree. A fourth-power Poincare correspondence converts the selected surface component to a primitive codimension-two class; its positive self-intersection gives an exact algebraic nonvanishing test. We complete a global control between nonisomorphic CM elliptic curves of discriminant $-20$, including actual degree-two and degree-three maps, all $447$ bounded Hom graphs, and a selected surface norm of $72$. A nonscalar elliptic-square control checks the trace normalization and distinguishes central from noncentral CM. The ingredients are classical; the contribution is their combined transport specification and verified realization tests. Degree-$110$ source multiplicities, quotient-polarization degrees, and graph algebras remain unevaluated. No new Hodge-conjecture existence case or general solution is claimed.
author: cm_symmetry_scout
title: Bounded Hom graphs and algebraic selection for CM surface transport
